chapters.title: Laying Plans
chapters.sourcePressure: The opening frames war as a life-or-ruin inquiry governed by five constant factors, seven comparative questions, adaptation to circumstance, deception, and many calculations before battle.
chapters.coreMove: Run the five-factor comparison before action so you know whether the field can support the move you want to make.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating planning as motivational goal-setting or a generic pros-and-cons list.

chapters.title: Waging War
chapters.sourcePressure: The source counts the cost of campaigns in chariots, armor, silver, exhausted weapons, drained households, supply wagons, forage, rewards, and the danger of prolonged war.
chapters.coreMove: Price delay in real resources so you stop confusing drawn-out effort with disciplined pursuit of victory.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the lesson into move fast at all costs or generic efficiency advice.

chapters.title: Attack by Stratagem
chapters.sourcePressure: The source ranks outcomes: take intact rather than destroy, break resistance without fighting, block plans and alliances before field battle, avoid sieges, respect force ratios, and protect military judgment from ignorant command.
chapters.coreMove: Break the opposing plan before you collide with the opposing force.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the idea to avoid conflict or be clever in a vague way.

chapters.title: Tactical Dispositions
chapters.sourcePressure: The source separates protection from attack, teaches that opportunity comes from the opponent, praises winning by making no mistakes, and links measurement through calculation to victory.
chapters.coreMove: Make defeat hard before you look for the moment that makes victory easy.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating defense as passivity or waiting for luck.

chapters.title: Energy
chapters.sourcePressure: The source explains command through subdivisions and signals, direct and indirect methods, inexhaustible combinations, simulated disorder backed by discipline, baits, picked men, and momentum like rolling stones.
chapters.coreMove: Combine simple direct and indirect moves so the system carries force that no single person has to supply alone.
chapters.commonMisread: Equating energy with hustle, charisma, or personal intensity.

chapters.title: Weak Points and Strong
chapters.sourcePressure: The source teaches arriving fresh, imposing your will, forcing movement, hiding your point of attack, dividing the opponent, and adapting like water to the ground and foe.
chapters.coreMove: Shape the contest so your strength meets their exposed weakness, not their prepared front.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating weakness as personal flaw-spotting or opportunistic bullying.

chapters.title: Maneuvering
chapters.sourcePressure: The source warns that maneuvering is difficult, weighs forced marches of a hundred, fifty, and thirty li, insists on local guides, signals, mood, strength husbanding, and leaving an outlet for a surrounded foe.
chapters.coreMove: Turn detours, timing, signals, and restraint into advantage without exhausting the force that has to arrive.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating maneuver as simply moving fast or outworking the opponent.

chapters.title: Variation in Tactics
chapters.sourcePressure: The source lists roads not to follow, armies not to attack, towns not to besiege, positions not to contest, commands not to obey, then ties tactical variation to blended advantage and disadvantage and five dangerous faults.
chapters.coreMove: Hold rules loosely enough to disobey a bad route, bad order, or bad temptation when the situation changes.
chapters.commonMisread: Using flexibility as an excuse for improvising without discipline.

chapters.title: The Army on the March
chapters.sourcePressure: The source teaches how to camp and observe: mountains, rivers, marshes, high sunny ground, ambush signs in birds, dust, trees, chariots, water-drawers, shifted flags, and discipline with humanity.
chapters.coreMove: Read terrain, weather, and small signs before they become orders you cannot ignore.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning observation into vague situational awareness without concrete signals.

chapters.title: Terrain
chapters.sourcePressure: The source classifies six kinds of terrain and six calamities caused by the general, then insists that enemy openness, your own readiness, and the nature of the ground all have to align.
chapters.coreMove: Match the decision to the ground and to your own condition before blaming fate or the opponent.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating terrain as external circumstances only, with no responsibility for command failures.

chapters.title: The Nine Situations
chapters.sourcePressure: The source names nine grounds, prescribes different actions for each, emphasizes solidarity deeper in hostile country, seized valuables, desperate ground, shuai-jan responsiveness, Wu and Yueh cooperating in a storm, and Marquis Wu mourning his troops.
chapters.coreMove: Change conduct as the human pressure of the ground changes, especially when danger can create unity or panic.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the nine situations into a static taxonomy instead of pressure-sensitive leadership.

chapters.title: The Attack by Fire
chapters.sourcePressure: The source names five fire attacks, insists on ready materials, dry weather, special wind days, five developments after fire starts, windward position, signal fires, and restraint against anger or pique.
chapters.coreMove: Use volatile force only when timing, materials, wind, and advantage line up, because damage cannot be called back.
chapters.commonMisread: Reading fire as aggression, escalation, or dramatic action rather than controlled irreversible force.
mustUseTerms: five ways of attacking with fire

chapters.title: The Use of Spies
chapters.sourcePressure: The source argues that a small outlay for intelligence prevents massive public loss, says foreknowledge comes from people rather than spirits or calculation, names five spy classes, values converted spies, secrecy, rewards, and historical servant-advisers behind dynastic rise.
chapters.coreMove: Pay for human foreknowledge before committing lives and resources to ignorance.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing spying to sneaky behavior, gossip, or data dashboards.
